gp.heading: Adjusted Gross Profit
gp.text:
We analyze our adjusted gross profit, which is a Non-GAAP measure, which we define as revenues less cost of sales, excluding impairment and depreciation of specialty rental assets to measure our financial performance. Please see “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” for a definition and reconciliation to the most comparable GAAP measure. We believe adjusted gross profit is a meaningful metric because it provides insight into the financial performance of our revenue streams without consideration of company overhead. Additionally, using adjusted gross profit gives us insight on factors impacting cost of sales, such as efficiencies of our direct labor and material costs. When analyzing adjusted gross profit, we compare actual adjusted gross profit to our budgets and internal projections and to prior period results for a given period in order to assess our performance.

We also use Non-GAAP measures such as EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, and Discretionary cash flows to evaluate the operating performance of our business. For a more in-depth discussion of the Non-GAAP measures, please refer to the "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" section.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, revenue related to the HFS – South segment represented approximately 44% of our revenue, revenue related to our Government segment represented 22% of our revenue, revenue related to the WHS segment represented 30% of our revenue, and All Other revenue represented 4% of our revenue.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company had three customers who accounted for 28%, 11% and 11% of total revenue, respectively, and our five largest customers accounted for approximately 63% of our total revenue.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company had three customers who accounted for 28 %, 11 % and 11 % of total revenues, respectively.
The largest customer accounted for 48 % of accounts receivable, while no other customer accounted for more than 10% of the accounts receivable balance as of December 31, 2025.
For the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company had one customer who accounted for 48 % of revenues.
The largest customer accounted for 43 % of accounts receivable, while no other customer accounted for more than 10% of the accounts receivable balance as of December 31, 2024 .
For the year ended December 31, 2023, the Company had one customer representing 62 % of revenues.
There were no single customers from the HFS – South segment for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 that represented 10% or more of the Company’s consolidated revenues.
Revenues from one customer within the WHS segment represented approximately 28 % of the Company’s consolidated revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025.

Revenues from one customer within the Government segment represented approximately 11 %, 48 %, and 62 % of the Company’s consolidated revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

Revenues from another customer within the Government segment represented approximately 11 %, 9.9 %, and 9.9 % of the Company’s consolidated revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
